inShort: A dinks to the middle, then short and wide. B hits the ATP, and A resets it back into the kitchen. 10 rounds in a row, then swap.
rules: A and B stand diagonally at the kitchen line, cross-court.
A dinks to the middle, then plays the next dink short and wide, close to the net: the ATP setup.
B moves out wide and hits the ATP around the post, one-handed or two-handed, whatever the time allows.
A defends: turns toward the ball, paddle low, and resets it soft into the kitchen.
Back to the middle and straight into the next round, no break.
10 rounds in a row, then swap roles.
tooEasy: A varies the angle and pace of the wide ball, so B has to read one hand or two. Even harder: A plays the rounds faster.
tooHard: A plays the wide ball wider and shorter, so the ATP gets easier.
goodLooksLike: B's ATP passes low around the post and lands in the court, and A's reset lands in the kitchen.
